proof_scope: In progress. R1778 defines the multiplicity-preserving symmetric generator probability measure rho and its actual convolution walk, proving A_(rho^(*n))f=T^n f for the existing finite symmetric average T on actual complex L2. For any symmetric linear map on a real inner-product space, unit f and 0<=r<=||Tf|| imply r^(2^m)<=||T^(2^m)f||. Completeness, boundedness and contraction are unnecessary in the linear-map version. SL(2,R) is locally compact by its closed matrix embedding. The explicit Frobenius ball B_eta={g:sum of four squared entry errors<eta^2} is open, contains identity for eta>0, and lies in a compact matrix-entry box. Its Haar mass is positive and finite. The normalized restricted Haar measure P_eta is therefore an actual probability kernel, with the explicit indicator density and almost-everywhere entry bounds. If a unit Schwartz u has Q_j(u)<=R, ||Tu||>=r>=0, 0<eta<=1/2 and 29*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta<=r^(2^m)/2, then ||A_(rho^(*(2^m))*P_eta)u||>=r^(2^m)/2.
